LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 6.3.1 FUTURE TIME (WILL/SHALL)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.3: Language Use 6.3.1 Future time (will/shall)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 6.3.1 Future time (will/shall), part of Strand 6 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How would you talk about things that will happen tomorrow or later?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Recognise sentences with words that express future time from a text.

2. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Recognise sentences with words that express future time from a text.
2. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 6.3.1 Future time (will/shall) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Communication: The learner’s ability to speak engagingly is enhanced as they use ‘will’/‘shall’ correctly to talk about future

time/events.

 Collaboration: Teamwork is enhanced as the learner actively participates in question and answer activity with peers using

‘shall’/’will’.

Values:
Responsibility is developed as the learner takes up roles in question and answer activity with peers.

Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner’s self-esteem is boosted as they use will/shall effectively in communication.
